deduplication.identityRule: An original invocation is identified by (window/scenario, startedUtc) where timestamps exist. Carried ledger rows (scenario 10-15 rows appear identically in the r4, r5, r7, r10, r11 and r12 ledgers) are counted once by startedUtc equality; all carried copies were compared and match. deduplication.carriedRowsNotDoubleCounted: Scenario 10 rows 1-6 and scenario 11 row 7 appear in 6 retained ledgers; window 13 rows 8-11 and window 14 row 12 appear in 3; each counted once here.
deduplication.crossCheckWithTerminalRecord: The terminal tranche's reported slice USD 0.213437388 equals this baseline's recipe + scenario11 + window13 + window14 subtotals exactly.
deduplication.limitsOfProof: startedUtc equality and exact carried-value equality establish identity where timestamps exist. Where neither exists (P4 era), identity rests on the one-to-one log mapping below; residual ambiguity is retained, not resolved by assumption.

knownLimitations: Values are provider-reported ledger observations, not an account-debit audit; actual billed amounts may differ.
The recipe-to-row mapping (which of R4-R8 corresponds to ledger rows 2-6) is not recorded in the ledger; rows are identified by startedUtc only. R1 is row 1 by the r3-window date.

Scenario 12 (window 12) records no new pipeline charge in the terminal ledger and its retained verification carries no cost fields; it is counted as zero new charge, matching the terminal record's arithmetic.
No historical ledger, log or window was executed or reopened to produce this baseline; all figures are read from retained records and their byte-identical promoted copies.
Logs named '(unpromoted)' are identified by filename only; the corresponding charge evidence is the promoted verification or ledger cited in the same row.
